decision: new repo depending on helios and reth crates, no fork
why: forking either carries 22k or 454k mostly-deleted lines; neither has a persistent known-key store
evidence: Notes/20261005 Partial-State Wallet Node Sketch.md; agent://HeliosAngle; agent://RethNetAngle

decision: target Sepolia Glamsterdam; fork time confirmed in both deps
why: helios gloas epoch 353024 and alloy-hardforks sepolia amsterdam both resolve to 1791294816 (2026-10-06 13:53:36 UTC)

decision: pin reth 7a5c817ab and helios 68e3d07 as git deps, copy helios ethereum_hashing patch
why: reth crates are git-only per its sdk docs; cargo patches do not propagate to dependents

decision: dependency spike: helios-ethereum + reth-network/downloaders/trie-common + revm 43 + alloy-evm 0.39 in one workspace
why: riskiest unknown was whether the two git dep trees co-resolve

decision: renamed project to chibi; repo now ~/Documents/Codes/chibi; crates will be chibi-*
architect arena with 3 structurally distinct runners: actor-owned node, pure value core, runner's choice
why: design it twice before code; the store and concurrency shape is the one-way door

decision: done predicate (live, after fork): on Sepolia with no execution RPC configured, chibi shows an account ETH balance, nonce, and one ERC-20 balance that match a public RPC oracle; watch updates them from BALs within a block; send simulates locally, broadcasts over devp2p, and confirms inclusion plus receipt status
why: falsifiable end-to-end check of every piece in the sketch; the public RPC is only the test oracle, never a wallet input

decision: done predicate (today, pre-fork): fmt and clippy clean; offline tests prove proof verification (present, absent, tampered), BAL application, store miss semantics and persistence, and simulation-with-misses equals full-state simulation; live Sepolia smoke covers light-client sync and devp2p header fetch, plus a snap/2 fetch if peers serve it
why: everything that does not need Amsterdam blocks gets proven today

decision: rigor: high on proof verification, BAL application and the store (they decide what the user sees); medium on CLI and wiring
why: a bug in the verified path silently shows wrong balances; a CLI bug is loud

decision: encode rust-best-practices as workspace clippy lints (unwrap deny, expect warn, print warn, wildcard enum arm warn, inline format args) and pin toolchain 1.98.1
why: rules enforced by the compiler beat rules repeated in prose to every implementer

decision: live Sepolia probe: devp2p header fetch plus single-key snap/2 GetAccountRange for the deposit contract, proof verified by reth AccountRangeDownloader
why: settle by observation whether snap/2 is testable before the fork
evidence: crates/spike/src/main.rs (throwaway); run output: 5 sessions, 1 snap/2 peer (Nethermind), header #11848105 hash_ok, account keccak 0xe745..0d9b nonce 1 balance 0
result: VERIFIED; matches cast nonce/balance against publicnode oracle; reth peers did not advertise snap/2

decision: requirements changed: local JSON-RPC for a browser wallet is the primary surface; no keys in chibi; network parameter with Sepolia default; init asks for watch-only addresses; track USDC
result: broadcast to arena runners mid-flight instead of restarting them

decision: seed token keys by running balanceOf(user) in the local EVM and tracking the keys it touched, instead of a per-token storage layout table
why: fetch-on-miss already discovers proxy and mapping slots for any ERC-20; a layout table would need a new entry per token
evidence: Sepolia USDC 0x1c7D..7238 is a zeppelinos proxy (impl slot 0x10d6..390b -> 0xd48f..baf7), checked with cast storage

decision: store advance without BALs re-verifies known keys at the new head, same path as reopen
why: Sepolia has no BALs until the fork and mainnet none until its own Glamsterdam; one code path covers both

decision: picked candidate B (pure core, thin async shell) as base; judge picked A 30 vs B 28
why: near tie; B has the shortest call chains (5-6 files, one task, 3 crates) and cheapest first slice; A's invariant wins (reopen reverify, wire types out of core, Optional BAL fetch) graft cleanly onto B, while A's actor and BAL roll-forward window add a task, ~15 handlers, and a bug the judge found (unchanged_since vacuous after window clear)

decision: grafts: from A reopen always reanchors and persisted values are display-only, core seam uses chibi reply types not reth snap messages, BAL fetch uses BalRequirement::Optional; from C persisted outbox written before broadcast, concurrency table, reorg and snap-window test faults; from judge never set helios cfg.checkpoint from the shipped default
why: each fixes a judge finding or closes a gap in B
